title: Intake Air Heater "A" Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the intake air heater. This part warms incoming air so a diesel engine starts easily in the cold.
symptoms: White smoke right after a cold start

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the intake air heater wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the intake air heater with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new intake air heater if it tests bad.

plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the intake air heater, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part warms incoming air so a diesel engine starts easily in the cold.

checks: Inspect the intake air heater wiring and connector for damage or corrosion

Test the intake air heater with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new intake air heater if it tests bad.

title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
plain: The computer has spotted a problem in the wiring circuit for the exhaust gas temperature sensor. This part (bank 1, sensor 1) measures exhaust heat to protect the turbocharger, catalytic converter or particulate filter.
symptoms: Possible reduced power on some diesel and turbo engines

causes.name: Damaged wiring or a loose or corroded connector
Blown fuse or missing power or ground to the sensor

checks: Inspect the exhaust gas temperature sensor wiring and connector for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check related fuses and confirm power and ground at the sensor
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new exhaust gas temperature sensor if it tests bad.

title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
plain: The signal from the exhaust gas temperature sensor is lower than it should ever be, which usually points to a wiring short or a failed sensor. This part (bank 1, sensor 1) measures exhaust heat to protect the turbocharger, catalytic converter or particulate filter.
symptoms: Possible reduced power on some diesel and turbo engines

causes.name: Problem with the sensor's reference voltage supply

checks: Inspect the wiring and connector for rubbing, damage or corrosion
Check reference voltage and ground at the connector with a meter
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new exhaust gas temperature sensor if it tests bad.

title: Cold Start "B" Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
plain: Right after a cold start, the "B" camshaft on bank 1 was further ahead (advanced) than the computer commanded. This is part of the variable valve timing system.
symptoms: Rough idle or hesitation right after a cold start

causes.name: Low, dirty or wrong-grade engine oil
Sticking or faulty variable valve timing solenoid

checks: Check the oil level and condition
Check for other camshaft timing or correlation codes
Test the timing solenoid and check cam timing on a scan tool
fix: Often an oil change with the correct oil or a new timing solenoid; a stretched chain or worn phaser needs a timing job.

title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit
plain: The computer has spotted a problem in the wiring circuit for the power steering pressure sensor. This part tells the computer when steering effort rises so it can bump the idle and avoid stalling.
symptoms: Idle may dip or the engine may stall when turning the wheel at low speed

causes.name: Damaged wiring or a loose or corroded connector
Blown fuse or missing power or ground to the sensor

checks: Inspect the power steering pressure sensor wiring and connector for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check related fuses and confirm power and ground at the sensor
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new power steering pressure sensor if it tests bad.

title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The power steering pressure sensor is sending a reading that doesn't make sense or doesn't match other sensors. This part tells the computer when steering effort rises so it can bump the idle and avoid stalling.
symptoms: Idle may dip or the engine may stall when turning the wheel at low speed

causes.name: Faulty or sluggish power steering pressure sensor
Low power steering fluid or a weak power steering pump
Wiring or connector problem skewing the reading

checks: Compare the power steering pressure sensor reading on a scan tool with real conditions
Check the power steering fluid level and look for leaks
Inspect the wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
fix: Usually a new power steering pressure sensor or repair of the underlying problem, after ruling out wiring.

title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Low Input
plain: The signal from the power steering pressure sensor is lower than it should ever be, which usually points to a wiring short or a failed sensor. This part tells the computer when steering effort rises so it can bump the idle and avoid stalling.
symptoms: Idle may dip or the engine may stall when turning the wheel at low speed

causes.name: Problem with the sensor's reference voltage supply

checks: Inspect the wiring and connector for rubbing, damage or corrosion
Check reference voltage and ground at the connector with a meter
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new power steering pressure sensor if it tests bad.

title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the power steering pressure sensor keeps cutting in and out or jumping around. This part tells the computer when steering effort rises so it can bump the idle and avoid stalling.
symptoms: Idle may dip or the engine may stall when turning the wheel at low speed

causes.name: Chafed wiring that shorts or opens over bumps

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data on a scan tool
Look for chafed wires near hot or moving parts
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new power steering pressure sensor if it tests bad.

title: System Voltage
plain: The computer sees the vehicle's electrical system voltage outside its normal range or missing at one of its inputs.
symptoms: Battery or charging warning light on

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery terminals or grounds
Blown fuse feeding the engine computer

checks: Test the battery and charging voltage
Clean and tighten the battery terminals and engine grounds
Check the fuse that powers the engine computer
fix: Usually a battery, alternator, cable or ground repair.

title: System Voltage Unstable
plain: The vehicle's electrical voltage is jumping around instead of holding steady.
symptoms: Battery or charging warning light on

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery terminals or grounds

checks: Check the battery terminals and engine grounds for tightness and corrosion
Watch charging voltage while turning on lights and the blower
Inspect the drive belt
fix: Usually a battery cable, ground or alternator repair.

title: System Voltage Low
plain: The computer sees the vehicle's electrical voltage below normal, which usually points to the battery or charging system.
symptoms: Battery or charging warning light on

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery cables or ground straps

checks: Test the battery and check that charging voltage is roughly 13.5 to 14.8 volts with the engine running
Clean and tighten the battery terminals and grounds
Inspect the serpentine belt and tensioner
Check for other charging system codes
fix: Most often a new alternator or battery, or a cable or ground repair.
drive: If there is only a stored code and the vehicle is operating normally, arrange a charging-system check and tell the shop which code was recorded.
test_first: Load test the battery, check charging voltage at the battery, inspect cables, grounds and the drive belt, and check for a parasitic drain before replacing the alternator or battery.
urgent_if: If the charging-system warning stays on while driving, lights are dimming, or steering assistance changes, pull over as soon as it's safe. Call roadside assistance and follow your owner's manual.

title: System Voltage High
plain: The computer sees the vehicle's electrical voltage above normal, which can overcharge the battery and stress electronics.
symptoms: Battery smelling of sulfur or swelling

causes.name: Poor battery voltage-sense connection or bad ground
Faulty battery current or temperature sensor
Recent jump start or battery charger hookup

checks: Measure charging voltage with the engine running
Check the alternator wiring and engine grounds
fix: Usually a new alternator or voltage regulator, or a ground repair.
drive: If there is only a stored code and the vehicle is operating normally, arrange a charging-system check and tell the shop which code was recorded.
urgent_if: If the charging-system warning stays on while driving, lights are dimming, or steering assistance changes, pull over as soon as it's safe. Call roadside assistance and follow your owner's manual.

title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input "A" Circuit
plain: The computer is seeing an incorrect signal from the cruise control multi-function switch input "A".
symptoms: Cruise control not working or cutting out

causes.name: Faulty cruise control switch on the steering wheel or stalk
Worn clockspring (the coiled wiring inside the steering wheel)

checks: Check whether the horn and other steering wheel buttons work
Watch the cruise switch signals on a scan tool while pressing each button
fix: Usually a new cruise control switch or clockspring.
